text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The boss of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) in crime-stricken Kiambu district, is threatened with death, if he does not leave the district within 20 days.
- Parliament lifts the 20-year-old ban on the export of mangrove poles.
- A new bill to register, regulate and control religious organisations has been drafted and will be taken to Parliament soon.
- Kenyan Michael Odenyo who had been held as a suspected hijacker of the Ethiopian plane that crashed into the Indian Ocean off the Comoros is scheduled to return to Kenya today (Thursday).
- Information Minister Johnstone Makau, is accused of sexually harassing women employees of Kenya Broadcasting Corporation.
- Small depositors of the collapsed Kenya Finance Bank will be paid their protected deposits on December 9, and not January 6, 1997, as earlier announced.
- The Kenya government and Britain sign two grant agreements amounting to about 1.1 billion shillings which will finance an HIV/AIDS Prevention and Care project.
